I've updated the memory store. The old note said to release by pushing a `vYYYY.MM.N` git tag and letting CI publish. I replaced it with a new note that says to use `make release`, and the new note officially supersedes the old one.

One problem: the `Makefile` in this checkout doesn't have a `release` target yet. It only has `test` and `test-fast`. The target may live on a branch that hasn't been merged, or it may still need to be written. Either way, `make release` would fail here right now. The new memory says to check that the target exists first, and it will be flagged if the `Makefile` changes.

I can write the target if you tell me what it should run, such as the tag format and the publish command.
